name: expiry_day_pattern_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-agent-3
thesis: F&O expiry days (weekly Thursday for NIFTY/BANK NIFTY, monthly last Thursday for stocks) exhibit distinct intraday patterns driven by options market makers' gamma hedging and pin risk. On expiry day: (1) indices tend to pin near the strike with maximum open interest ('max pain'), (2) gamma exposure amplifies moves away from max pain in the morning but dampens them in the afternoon, (3) the last 90 minutes see accelerated theta decay forcing option sellers to unwind hedges, creating directional moves. The strategy: BUY_CE/BUY_PE to trade mean-reversion toward max pain in the morning, then trade breakouts in the last 90 minutes as gamma hedging unwinds. The inefficiency exists because most retail traders trade options directly on expiry day (hoping for lottery payoffs) rather than trading the predictable underlying patterns created by options dynamics.

other: max pain strike (computed from option chain OI)

indicators.name: max_pain_strike
indicators.formula: strike_price that minimizes sum(OI_call * max(0, strike - S) + OI_put * max(0, S - strike)) across all strikes

indicators.name: net_gamma
indicators.formula: sum(OI_call * gamma_call - OI_put * gamma_put) across all strikes

conditions: (expiry_phase == 'morning_pin' AND distance_to_max_pain < -30 bps) -- below max pain, expect pin rally, BUY_CE
OR (expiry_phase == 'afternoon_unwind' AND close > high_of_last_360_bars AND net_gamma > 0) -- gamma squeeze up, BUY_CE
long.confirmation: morning: close > close[24] for 24 bars (2 min bounce starting). afternoon: volume_surge > 1.5

conditions: (expiry_phase == 'morning_pin' AND distance_to_max_pain > 30 bps) -- above max pain, expect pin pullback, BUY_PE
OR (expiry_phase == 'afternoon_unwind' AND close < low_of_last_360_bars AND net_gamma < 0) -- gamma squeeze down, BUY_PE
short.confirmation: morning: close < close[24] for 24 bars (2 min). afternoon: volume_surge > 1.5

entry.entry_price: market order on ATM CE/PE on confirmation

exit.target: morning_pin: price reaches max_pain_strike (option premium target). afternoon_unwind: 30 bps from entry
exit.stop_loss: morning_pin: 15 bps beyond max pain distance (diverging). afternoon_unwind: 15 bps from entry
exit.time_stop: morning trades exit after 24 bars (120 seconds). afternoon trades exit by 15:25
exit.signal_exit: max_pain_strike shifts by >0.5% (OI structure changed, thesis invalidated)

risk.position_sizing: 1 lot per trade in index options

filters.vix_filter: India_VIX > 12 AND < 25 (need some vol for gamma effects but not too much chaos)
filters.volume_filter: index option volume > 1.2x normal (confirmed active expiry)
filters.trend_filter: morning: contrarian toward max pain. afternoon: trend-following breakout
filters.event_filter: ONLY on expiry days (weekly or monthly)
other_filters: skip if max_pain_strike has shifted >1% from previous day's close (unusual OI buildup)

edge.edge_decay_risk: Medium -- expiry day patterns are increasingly discussed on Indian trading social media, but the two-phase approach (pin + unwind) is more sophisticated than the simple 'sell options on expiry' strategy most retail traders use.

mechanism: On expiry days at 5-second frequency, gamma effects create rapid, predictable micro-movements. In the morning, the index oscillates around max pain with 10-30 second overshoots that revert -- at 5s resolution we can detect these overshoots (distance_to_max_pain crossing -30 bps) and enter BUY_CE/BUY_PE for the snap-back within 5-20 seconds. In the afternoon, the gamma unwind creates explosive moves as market makers' delta hedging flips from dampening to amplifying. At 5s resolution, we detect the breakout bar (close > high_of_last_360_bars) 20-40 seconds before it would register on a 1-min chart, capturing the initial surge of the gamma squeeze via option premium. Theta decay on expiry day means ATM options are extremely sensitive to underlying moves (high gamma), making even 10-20 point index moves produce outsized option returns.
adaptation_notes: Adapted from 1-min index futures strategy to 5-sec index option strategy. Key changes: (1) Universe remains NIFTY/BANKNIFTY but execution changed from index futures to index options (BUY_CE/BUY_PE), (2) Lookback for high/low reference adjusted from 30 bars to 360 bars (equivalent 30 min at 5s), (3) Bounce confirmation changed from 2 bars (2 min) to 24 bars (2 min at 5s), (4) Max pain recompute interval changed from 30 min to 360 bars, (5) Hold time compressed from 15-45 min to 5-120 seconds -- scalping the gamma-driven micro-moves, (6) On expiry day, 0DTE ATM options have extreme gamma making them the ideal instrument for capturing these short-lived moves, (7) Entry/exit now reference option premium (BUY_CE/BUY_PE) instead of futures BUY/SHORT.
weaknesses: Max pain calculation requires full option chain data and is sensitive to OI changes during the day. Stale OI data (even 30-min old) can mislead.
With weekly expiries, every Thursday is an expiry day but gamma effects are smaller for weekly options (less OI). Monthly expiry effects are stronger but only 12 per year.
The afternoon gamma squeeze can be violent and fast -- if the stop loss is too tight (15 bps), it may get hit before the squeeze completes.
prior_art: Ni, Pearson & Poteshman (2005) 'Stock Price Clustering on Option Expiration Dates'. Avellaneda & Lipkin (2003) 'A market-induced mechanism for stock pinning'. In India, expiry day effects are widely discussed by practitioners but limited academic study exists.
notes: Adapted for 5-second NIFTY50/BANKNIFTY index option trading. On expiry day, 0DTE ATM options are the ideal instrument due to extreme gamma -- small index moves produce large option premium changes. Focus on NIFTY/BANKNIFTY weekly options with maximum OI for strongest gamma effects.
